chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, I have transmitted it from my father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Al-Hadith ibn Abdullah and Al-Himyari together, from Ayyub ibn Nuh.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the author's father (often Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah in this context)
key_terms.أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ: Ayyub ibn Nuh, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both, a phrase of respect for the two narrators
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key narrator

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for Ayyub ibn Nuh's hadiths in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq establishes the reliability of Ayyub ibn Nuh’s narrations by tracing them through two independent chains via his father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, highlighting the scholarly rigor of the Qum school. This specific emphasis on Ayyub, a key figure in early Shia hadith transmission, underscores the importance of verifying the 'Thiqa' (reliable) status of narrators to ensure the authenticity of Imami jurisprudence.
